entries.title: Civic identity security hardened and public Citizen Directory opened
entries.summary: Following a citizen-led security review, certificate identifiers were removed from public civic APIs and are no longer accepted as proof for account activation, restoration, or credential changes. New civic accounts instead receive a separate one-time activation code whose plaintext is shown only during issuance and whose digest is consumed atomically at first sign-in. A new Citizen Directory now lists only profiles whose citizens explicitly selected broad public visibility.

metadata.firstActivation: Separate random one-time code retained only as a digest and consumed atomically
metadata.credentialRecovery: Administrator-assisted when existing password verification is unavailable
changes: Certificate identifiers redacted from population, citizen-register, and ledger API responses
Certificate identifiers rejected as activation and recovery proof
New one-time activation codes separated from civic certificates
Activation code consumption made single-use under concurrent requests
Population ticker and Citizen Register linked to opted-in public profiles
Private portal and editorial analytics authorization preserved server-side
